Sean/Ben/Priyom — forwarding the Avalon snapshot. Quick verbal model from my side (assumptions inline):

Summary assumption set (starter):
- Traffic shape: sustained baseline 40–60k tokens/sec, campaign microbursts to 95k that last ~5–20 minutes (customer note says "burst to 95k during campaigns"). If those are minute-level, we treat as microburst.
- Average prompt length: 220 tokens; mean generated tokens per request: 180 => average round-trip ~400 tokens
- Working model: Llama-family 34B-equivalent (customer has not pinned; assume full-precision 16-bit fallback path)
- KV cache hit: 18% as provided

Rough tokens/sec to GPU mapping (conservative):
- Baseline 50k tokens/sec sustained => ~8 RTX-8000-equivalent GPUs with batching and latency-targeted policies (assuming optimized kernels and 1.6–2.0 ms/token effective)
- For 95k sustained => ~14 GPUs (slab sizing)
- Microbursts: if bursts are 5–20m, we recommend burst-capacity add-on (additional 6 GPUs reserved for buffering) rather than full commit if they can't commit yet.

SLO fit notes:
- 200ms median inference is aggressive for 1,200 token requests unless you leverage aggressive quantization + tight batching. For large requests, p95 can push >500ms on compact rigs. Recommend: define SLOs as p50/p95 inference and allow streaming start-of-response (improves perceived latency).

Next steps I propose:
- Priyom, can you run a quick tokens/sec->GPU microbench using their sample (I can extract 50/95 token-length percentiles) and share a 2‑sheet workbook: "sizing" + "cost bands"?
- Sean: propose a 30-min call tomorrow 09:30–10:00 PT to confirm burst durations and model family pin.

Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Fwd: Q4 surge planning — quick sizing assumptions

Marissa / team — ran a quick microbench against a 34B-like variant using Avalon sample shapes. Notes below (attached CSV contains the run outputs):

Bench assumptions:
- Model run: open 34B profile (no strict pin) with 4-bit quant path and kernel selection tuned for 1k token sequences
- Batch policy: continuous batching with latency floor 40ms, max batch size tuned for 200ms median target
- Measured effective tokens/sec per GPU: 6.8k tokens/sec (median) at 200ms median for 400-token round-trip; tail latency grows with request length

Derived sizing (safety factor 1.25 to account for multi-tenant variance):
- Sustained 50k tps => 50k / 6.8k = 7.35 -> round up to 8 GPUs -> apply 1.25 safety -> 10 GPUs
- Sustained 95k tps => 95k / 6.8k = 13.97 -> 14 GPUs -> safety -> 18 GPUs
- Microburst buffer (for 95k peaks lasting 10–20m): add 6–8 burst GPUs (on-demand or reserved-burst pool)

Latency/quality tradeoffs:
- To reliably hit 200ms median on 1,200 token requests we'd need to either: 1) pin a lower-latency smaller model with ensemble reranking, or 2) accept streaming-first-token and longer tail. Both have cost/quality tradeoffs.

Proposal for customer-facing options (we'll present):
A) Conservative Dedicated commit: 12 GPUs reserved (covers baseline + modest headroom) + 8 GPU burst pool (auto-burst) — lower monthly commit, good for phased rollout
B) Performance commit: 20 GPUs reserved (covers sustained 95k with safety) — higher commit, better p95 outcomes
C) Hybrid: 10 GPUs reserved + streaming-first + model quant program + 10 GPU burst capacity (balanced cost/latency)

I'll attach the raw run CSV and a quick workbook outline to the proposal.

Priyom
Applied ML / Inference Performance, Redwood Inference
